text:
maria: Kicking off post-provision observability checks for af-south2 GPU cluster. TF apply completed, collectors deployed. Who can run a quick smoke? :eyes:
kevin: I can. Which collectors did we land — Vector or Fluentd? Also, any custom parsers for the NVIDIA driver logs?
satya: We deployed Vector as the primary agent (OTLP + Loki+Prometheus exporters). Fluentd only for legacy S3 forwarding. Driver logs are routed through a small grok filter in Vector to extract gpu_id/driver_version.
jess: Stack deployed: Prometheus operator, Thanos sidecar (for object storage), Grafana, Loki, Tempo, Vector DaemonSet. Loki ingestion configured to use a 7d compressed retention by default.
maria: Great. Smoke checklist (short):
  1) kubectl get pods -n observability (all Running)
  2) Prometheus /metrics scrape check for node-exporter + kube-state-metrics
  3) Loki: tail a recent GPU driver log and ensure labels (gpu_id) present
  4) Grafana: load default dashboards and check data-src connections
  5) Alerts: ensure alertmanager is contactable and sample alert fires in test route
kevin: Running 1) now:
```
kubectl -n observability get pods
NAME                                   READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
prometheus-0                           2/2     Running   0          6m
vector-ds-abcde                        1/1     Running   0          5m
loki-0                                 1/1     Running   0          5m
grafana-6f7d                            1/1     Running   0          4m
```
All good except node-exporter daemonset not present on gpu nodes (only on infra nodes).
satya: Ah, we forgot the node-exporter GPU label selector. The daemonset is currently filtered to node-role.kubernetes.io/infra. For GPU health we need it on nodes with label "accelerator=gpu". I'll patch the DS.
jess: Patch command:
```
kubectl -n observability patch daemonset node-exporter -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"nodeSelector":{"accelerator":"gpu"}}}}}'
```
kevin: Patch applied. Re-checking metrics endpoint: curl to Prometheus target healthy for gpu-node-3:
```
curl -sS http://prometheus.observability.svc:9090/api/v1/targets | jq '.data.activeTargets[] | select(.labels.instance=="gpu-node-3:9100")'
```
Returns target with lastScrape=23s, health="up".
maria: Loki check next. I will tail a recent driver crash log and confirm labels.
maria: `kubectl -n gpu-logs logs -l app=gpu-driver -c driver -f | head -n 50` shows entries. Sending sample to Loki via Vector and verifying labels in Grafana Explore: query `{job="vector", gpu_id=~".*"}` shows recent lines with gpu_id and node labels. :thumbsup:
satya: Note: driver logs are verbose at INFO level — we should ensure a pipeline stage that drops repeated heartbeat lines to keep ingestion cost down. Add a transform in Vector with a throttle/drop. I opened a PR for a rate-limit transform.
jess: Grafana dashboards: I imported the GPU summary dashboard (custom) and linked metrics:
- gpu.utilization (prometheus: `sum by(gpu) (nvidia_gpu_utilization_percent)`)
- gpu.memory.used (prometheus: `nvidia_gpu_memory_used_bytes`)
- node.fs.inodes_free (for disk pressure alerts)
kevin: Alerting quick tests: created a synthetic alert rule for node:FakeHighTemp (for testing route). Firing it now.
deploy-bot: alertmanager: route "oncall-sre" notified (silence_id=none)
satya: I see it in Alertmanager UI. Route matched SRE oncall and PagerDuty. Good.
maria: Couple of follow-ups before handoff to platform:
- Add node-exporter to gpu nodes permanently in the TF module (avoid patching).
- Add Vector transform to drop repetitive INFO lines (save ~30-40% Loki ingestion during boot storms).
- Update Grafana dashboard variables for region=af-south2 and GPU pool names.
- Add alert templates: GPU temperature > 90C for 2m, GPU mem usage > 92% for 5m, node disk inode pressure > 80% for 3m.
satya: I'll open an infra ticket with TF diff and the Vector transform config. Sample transform YAML snippet: 
```
transforms.drop_heartbeats:
  type: filter
  condition: '!(.message contains "HEARTBEAT")'
```
kevin: Also a note on cost: Loki ingestion spiked when we bootstrapped all nodes. Recommend temporary Alert: loki_ingestion_rate > 500MB/min triggers auto-slowdown (switch to tail-only for driver logs) and a PagerDuty page to alert platform for potential bill risk.
jess: Agreed. I'll add a Grafana alert at the datasource level and an Alertmanager route with a cost-suppression window we can enable during large provisioning.
maria: Final sanity: can someone validate Thanos uploads to object store? I ran `thanos bucket inspect` earlier — returned expected blocks.
kevin: Confirmed: `thanos bucket inspect --objstore.config-file=/etc/thanos/s3.yaml` returns 12 blocks and last compaction 2h ago.
maria: OK passing this to platform (jess) for dashboards, alert templates, and long-term retention policy. Assigning follow-ups in the infra board. Thanks everyone. :party_parrot:
